messages.content: Hi friends! I'm currently considering the (probably terrible) idea of playing a Monad in the next season because I have a really cool character concept I think would be fun to explore. That being said, I've never seen one played so I wanted to think through it with anyone interested. More in the 🧵 if that's you. Thank you!!

Okay, so first up is trying to think about what the Monad frame is useful for (and not). This is probably where I need the most help. I'll put separate thoughts in separate entries to facilitate replies.

From what I understand, what Monads ARE good at is managing incoming damage (between the power that lets them add to and shift condition monitors and the power that lets them heal. Side question: I don't see anywhere that you can't just keep using this power to heal yourself, but that might be under healing itself). 

If that understanding is right, I think it lends itself towards a street sam. Supporting this seems to be that unlike magic and resonance, nanite volume doesn't decrease as your essence drops.

Oh, and Adrenal Control. Between this and healing, you're basically up or dead.

Next, I want to think about what I *think* might be traps in the Monad frame, really to make sure I'm thinking about this fully. First might be thinking Monads make decent tech characters. Without access to programs, agents, sprites, complex forms, or anything else they certainly have hands tied behind their backs. That being said, you should be able to get to "respectable" values versus NPC targets with minimal investment, at least for normal and veteran play.

Next potential trap might be the physical and mental attribute boosts. Since the amount boosted is net hits on a nanite volume test, which cannot be higher than 6 at start per SRMG, these are ~2 points improvement on average. Same for trading NV for minor actions, which trade 5 minutes of access to that NV for a single round of 1-2 extra minors.
Tech blast - why would you ever take this, unless you just didn't take the monad matrix attributes power and couldn't otherwise data spike?

Tech Infestation as written also seems to be a trap, because this doesn't say that you're specifically facing the FW of the device itself and not the PAN. So using your NV x2 will rapidly get kicked in the teeth by anything of narrative import, and for anything not of narrative import you can just do things normally.
so .... let me elaborate 🙂
(I was hoping to draw your interest)

healing thus far is not regulated which seems a mistake .. as the monad healing stems from its NV which is considered "awakened" it should count as magical healing which would limit it to once per set of injuries
but so far nothing has been decided (though i made a case to Rev0 about this)
as for the boosts .. they are valid if you dont have any other boosts (ware/ spells)
extra minors stay for the same time slot as boosts
there are two ways of gaining extra minors: Phys boost and extra actions .. allowing you to get +6 minors in the first turn you activate
after that its back to having 5 at the start of the turn
tech blast is a waste if you plan to have any matrix skills
oh interesting. I didn't realize these were separate and potentially stacking sources of minors.
tech infestation however is way better then it looks at the start
for it can also control purely mechanical devices not only hackable ones
also it is not subject to OS
heavily defended stuff is mostly beyond your capability unless you hit like 10 NV
but its the creepy i insert nanites and control the device (which usually has like DR2 and thus only FW 2) until i choose to release
technically this could also be done with hostile cyberware/ bioware (that cant be hacked at all normally)

I was wondering where you were going with tech infestation. I agree it's flavorful, and since monads don't really have a toolkit to monitor or manage OS (no baby monitor, no cleaner, just the matrix action to reboot your persona?) avoiding OS might be useful. 

IDK if I would try hacking cyberware/bioware at the table, mostly because I don't want to slow gameplay down with what some might construe as a creative interpretation of rules.
yeah its more of a scare against players hacking their bioware (and gets monads some respect)

for the starting 6 powers I was eyeing:
- monad toughness,
- rapid healing, 
- adrenal control,
- matrix attributes, 
- physical boost, and
- mental boost.
i wouldnt take the matrix attributes
those just make you a target ... you cant form networks so its personal only not even PAN
💯 I would use this as a GM against PCs, because as written I don't feel like Monads live up to the fear of them we had in 5e.
phys/mental boost as needed (ware)
can you protect your own cyberware with this persona? I guess not since you can't join your own ware to the persona?
my choices are: Toughness, Tox Res, action use, tech infest, rapid healing, possibly resculpt (if i dont have nanite hives) or phys/ mentalboost
no
its only for hacking
or matrix perception
whenever i play a monad i usually make him a secondary decker/rigger
With primary being?
because the quality hardened lets you absorb matrix damage as Stun damage to protect your stuff and healing also works in VR
rigger/face infiltrator (resculpt/mental boost)
my monad ended up as Street sam
cause having something akin to regeneration was cool
right. That's where I was heading too, a street sam monad. I was hoping to be able to defend my own ware, but that seems like a major area I need to rethink.
unless your defense is a good offense.
well save up money and get a good RCC or MTOC ... that is usually enough to protect your gear
That's very actionable. It'll be an M-TOC because I sorta did the rigger thing with my current char. I've never played an 'honest' street sam.
Ok, I think I'm in the basic ballpark. Thank you Oli!!
anytime 🙂
though don't hate me when the char comes out, but I'll probably take Matrix attributes anyway to support the AI part of the CFD.
There's a 2083 SRM with some monads in it - do you want to play against some first?
One more thing to add, high edge helps with NV rolls, pre edge 6 more dice is quite vital for some rolls ... However you cant score more net hits than NV
I always want to play!
That being said, we have plenty of time until next season so if this happens that's great. You should prioritize what sparks joy for you too!
